title: When Detection Depends on Who Is Detected
summary: Work through When Detection Depends on Who Is Detected.

sections: When Detection Depends on Who Is Detected
From a detection gap to a stopping gap

blocks.md: This lesson follows **When Detection Depends on Who Is Detected** in *Responsible Physical AI* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Responsible Physical AI, § When Detection Depends on Who Is Detected
blocks.md: A machine that earns open-floor permission on aggregate obstacle-detection metrics can still fail systematically on specific groups of people sharing the aisle or roadway. Buolamwini and Gebru found that commercial face-analysis systems misclassified darker-skinned women far more often than lighter-skinned men, and that the benchmarks used to evaluate them contained few of the people they failed on. Pedestrian detection shows the same pattern.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Detection gaps become stopping gaps matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A group of people a detector sees less often needs more frames before detection can be relied on, so a stop sized for the best-detected group loses distance before braking and strikes the other group with speed and energy that follow from the distance lost, and each group's sample must be large enough for its interval to resolve the gap.

questions.q: The section **When Detection Depends on Who Is Detected** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A group of people a detector sees less often needs more frames before detection can be relied on, so a stop sized for the best-detected group loses distance before braking and strikes the other group with speed and energy that follow from the distance lost, and each group's sample must be large enough for its interval to resolve the gap.

People protect themselves by predicting where a machine will go, so motion that reveals its goal early and explicit signals let them yield sooner, and signals are shown only where measured detection supports the trust they invite.
An operating permit carries a duty to report incidents completely and on time, so a permit can be withdrawn for a withheld or incomplete record as well as for the motion it describes.

Automation moves a task's labor into rescue, sweeping, monitoring, and data collection, and creates records that could be used to score workers, so a deployment counts the labor it moves and bars uses of its safety records that were never declared.
